the method of conditioning and the method of testing affect the magnitude of a taste aversion.
the method of conditioning and testing can influence the magnitude of taste aversion learning.

the role of taste in food selection.
the role of the amygdala in the formation of conditioned taste aversions, which are learned associations between the taste of a food and its consequences.

the strength of a learned association is determined by a combination of the conditioning and testing methods.
both methods of conditioning can produce taste aversion learning, but the method of testing is critical in determining the strength of the learned association.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method of conditioning and the method of testing affect the strength of taste aversion learning.
the method of conditioning and testing can affect taste aversion strength and that these effects are dependent upon the similarity between the conditioning and testing context.
when the context at testing is similar to the context at conditioning, the strength of the flavor-drug association depends on the method of testing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method used to test the strength of an aversion may influence the results obtained.
the method of testing should be carefully considered in studies of taste aversion conditioning.
when the method of conditioning is different from the method of testing, the strength of the learned association depends on the similarity of contextual cues at conditioning and testing.
